newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends limit down, OSB lumber limit up.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends limit down, OSB lumber limit up.

text.p: CME lumber futures ended as much as the limit down of $10.00 per thousand board feet on pressure linked to slow cash trade while Oriented Strand Board (OSB) lumber ended higher to limit up on news of a fire at one mill, traders said.
Lumber closed $10.00 to $3.10 per tbf higher with July up limit at $373.50 and September up the limit at $363.00.
July OSB ended up the $10.00 per 1,000 square foot limit at $148.50 while other months finished $4.90 to $5.00 higher.
Adequate product offerings and expectations of further weakness in cash lumber markets offset technical support and lumber fell the limit by midday, traders said.
The Canfor mill closings announcement provided support on Monday "but you have no follow through and cash prices are right back down," said Curt Cunningham, president of Pacific Futures Trading.
Cunningham said mills are generally asking around $360 but lumber could trade as low as $350.

Other analysts also cited the slow cash trade and expect declining prices, especially with the Canfor mill closings now considered bearish. Mills do not normally shut down in June but close in July and August due to fire hazards. Closing mills now shows demand is lagging and production too large, they said.

"The cash market never really reacted to the two-day rally in futures," said Neil Schmaedick, Smith Barney Forest Products analyst. "Particularly now, what with futures did today, cash is probably going to print lower - if it doesn't tomorrow if certainly will on Friday."
"We're looking at maybe making a new low for cash for the year," Schmaedick added.

Prudential Securities, Saul Stone and Lind-Waldock notably bought early. Further losses were seen in lumber Wednesday as the July option closed synthetically at $368, another $5.50 lower, pit sources said.
OSB lumber surged the limit when buying prompted by reports of fire destroying an OSB mill met little resistance. Iowa Grain notably bought July on the rally, traders said.
Malette Quebec Inc confirmed that its Timmins, Ontario strandboard mill closed after a fire Monday night.
